repair_actions: Bind repository identity to material the executing checkout cannot author: detached signature over the resolver module and trust policy verified against an out-of-band public key, or an external attestation the candidate checkout cannot mint. Fixed slug, numeric repository id and exact-commit API attestation are insufficient while the whole checkout is attacker-controlled.
Either make TRUST_ANCHOR_COMMIT load-bearing (verify resolver and policy bytes against that immutable anchor rather than against the artifact head) or remove it; today it is fetched and never used.

Extend the byte-anchored set, or canonical-byte loading, to every surface used to produce a PASS: the deterministic harness, the G runtime port request and output schemas, the E capability manifest schema, and the legacy S31 resolver module.
Enforce the G request and G output schemas in the S38 validation path so undeclared surface fails closed as it already does at F.
Represent historical identities explicitly: revision+path+blob+sha256 pins for every historical revision the evidence path resolves, not only the one archival fixture.

Remove the hard liveness dependency on the unauthenticated GitHub REST API, or document an authenticated and reproducible attestation path, so an independent reviewer can reproduce the result without an IP-shared quota.
remaining_risks: Deterministic PASS evidence is only as strong as the checkout that produced it; the producer harness itself is not byte-anchored.

Historical pin coverage currently holds by byte coincidence: the exercised paths still exist unchanged at the candidate head. A lawful rename or delete would reopen the same gap IR-006 found.
